reason: A shape quality, curved (PATO_0000406), not a structure. In '4–6 curved pairs of lateral veins' the bearer is lateral leaf vein (PO_0006011) and the count is of vein pairs. 'Curved muero' is a curved mucro, Spanish 'mucrón'. The 2026-11-14 review treated 'recurved' and 'keeled' the same way.

target: corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006) part_of disk flower (PO_0025332), pattern 12
reason: The lobes of a disc floret are the lobes of its corolla. Both classes exist, and pattern 12 expresses part of a qualified whole. This is the same mapping as 'disk lobe' in the 2026-11-14 review.

Narrower: a reduced cauline leaf (Habenaria, Erica) or an involucral leaf (Spermacoce) that looks like a bract. 'Bract-like' is a comparison on the leaf, not a different organ. Scale leaf (PO_0006003) fits the orchid uses, but its definition ties it to buds and rhizomes and it does not fit the Spermacoce head leaves, so the general class is safer.

Narrower: in Passifloraceae (Adenia, Basananthe) the floral corona (FLOPO_0985020) is divided into threadlike segments. The 2026-11-14 review mapped 'corona segment' to corona lobe, and the threadlike shape is a quality of the segment.

Narrower: in Cymopterus and Pediomelum the pseudoscape is the elongate, mostly underground stem between the root crown and the cluster of leaves at ground level. PO stem already carries caudex and scape as synonyms. Only one genus group in two related floras uses it, so a new class is not justified.

A counting frame ('secondary nerves 6–12 on a side'): the count per side of the midrib, not a structure. The bearer is the preceding part, usually secondary leaf vein (PO_0020140), counted per half-lamina.

target: leaf lamina margin (PO_0025009) of non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075), pattern 12, on the postical (ventral) side
reason: A liverwort term (e.g. Plagiochila): the leaf margin on the ventral side, toward the substrate. config/bearer_positions.tsv has no ventral/dorsal (postical/antical) position yet, and PATO has only the relational 'ventral to'. Adding a postical/antical pair there is the rule-level fix, and it should not be a new class.
Exact: the Spanish/Portuguese spelling of pistillode. PO already has 'pistillodium' as a synonym.
Narrower: an extrafloral nectary on the petiole (petiole, PO_0020038). PO already lists 'petiolar gland' as a synonym of extrafloral nectary.

A row is an arrangement, not a structure. '3–5 rows of epidermal cells' gives the number of layers or series of plant epidermal cell (PO_0004013). This follows 'rows of bristle' in the 2026-11-23 review.

target: spine leaf (PO_0025173), part of areole bud (PO_0025353), position in the series: central; count per areole (counted part per unit)
reason: Same as 'central spine' in the 2026-11-14 review. 'Per areole' is the counting unit, not part of the bearer.
Exact: a sorus is a cluster of sporangia. The elongate clusters measured here (20–45 × 1–4 mm) are linear sori. This matches 'soral line' → sorus in the 2026-11-14 review.

A disjunction of two element types (Vernonia, Tridax pappus). The count belongs to the pappus elements of pappus (PO_0025393), but the word itself is a fragment 'scales or bristles' and does not name one class. The 2026-11-14 review rejected 'teeth or lobe' for the same reason; the statements should be regrounded to the pappus.

Narrower: a leaf in the relation 'subtends' (as 'pistillate scale' in the 2026-11-14 review). In the Amelanchier examples ('1 or 2 subtended by a leaf') the count belongs to the subtended pedicels or flowers, not to the leaf. Those statements must not be attached to the leaf.

target: pattern 10 (ratio to another part), with the sulci (grooves) of the Mirabilis fruit as the second term
reason: A ratio expression: rib width as a multiple of the furrow width. The 2026-11-14 review treated 'times tube', 'times petiole' and 'times lobe' the same way.

Narrower. In every source (Mentzelia laevicaulis 'margin lobes 14–44', Solanum defensum 'lobes 3–6 on each side') these are lobes of a pinnately lobed leaf margin. Medium because the word alone does not name the organ, so the rule should only apply when the leaf is the context.
Exact: the tube formed by connate stamen filaments is the staminal tube.

target: phyllome lamina vein (PO_0025348) part of bract (PO_0009055), bearer_container PO_0009055
reason: The keel of a grass or sedge bract is its prominent midvein ridge, not PO keel (PO_0025327), which is the legume petal keel. This follows 'glume keel' and 'palea keel' in the 2026-11-23 review.

target: bract margin (PO_0025011) of flower bract (PO_0009034) subtending a pistillate flower (PO_0025599), pattern 12
reason: The 2026-11-14 review grounded 'pistillate scale' (Carex) as a flower bract subtending a pistillate flower. The margin is a region of it, and PO has bract margin.

The plicae (folds) between the corolla lobes, as in Gentiana, are described with margins that are erose, denticulate or entire. The corolla plica class was added after the 2026-11-14 review, so these describe the edge region of that class.

Narrower: in Cleidion and Mallotus these are the flat, spot-like glands near the base of the leaf blade, which are extrafloral nectaries. 'Maculate' (spot-like, flush with the surface) is their shape, not a different organ.

target: corolla limb (FLOPO_0986012) part_of ray flower (PO_0025331), pattern 12
reason: Same as 'ray lamina' in the 2026-11-14 review. It is not PO ligule (PO_0020105), the grass leaf ligule.

target: warty (PATO_0001361) on the carrying structure; the count gives the number of warts
reason: Warts are surface relief, already expressed by the quality warty on the bearer (leaf teeth in Chrysosplenium, the Adenia organ). PO tubercle (PO_0025352) is the cactus podarium and does not fit. Prefer the rule to a 'wart' class.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) on the apex of the leaf sheath (PO_0020104): region apex
reason: Same as 'oral seta' in the 2026-11-14 review (bamboo sheath shoulders). 'Leaf' only says which sheath, as opposed to the culm sheath.

target: laminal cell (FLOPO_0986100) at the leaf shoulder (the transition from sheathing base to limb) of non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075), position lower (FLOPO_0991377)
reason: Microcampylopus (Dicranaceae) is a moss, and the shoulder cells are laminal cells where the leaf base narrows into the limb. Only one genus uses the term, so it should not become a class. Low because the 'shoulder' region has no class and the position depends on the literature for this genus.
The pyrene class exists, and the apex is a region the patterns already express.
Exact: lobes on the margin of the corona are corona lobes ('margin with 5 threadlike lobes'). The count and shape attach to that class.

The sources mix organs: the united lateral petals of Impatiens, the pinna lobes of the fern Microlepia, and an Espeletia structure. The 2026-11-14 review rejected 'apical lobe', 'side lobe' and 'middle lobe' for the same reason.
Exact in use: veinlets enclosed in a vein areole (leaf lamina areole, PO_0025392) that end freely inside it, as in the areolate venation of ferns ('each areole with 1 or 2 included veinlets').
